messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — High 5xx rate from NLB in euc2 (targetgroup tg-ingress-euc2). Alert ID: #INC-2615
ops-bot: Symptoms: 502/504 surge, connection reset counts rising, downstream retries increasing.

maya: I’m looking — paging @oncall-sre. First signs at 08:12UTC, rolling 1m error rate 12% -> 45% for ingress.
ben: Confirming from metrics: envoy_upstream_rq_5xx{region="euc2"} spiked. TCP reset/sec on NLB backend nodes up x6.
claire: Any recent deploys? Checked deploys, nothing to euc2 in last 2 hours.

oncall-sre: Ack. I’m on it. Gathering health of targetgroup tg-ingress-euc2.
infra-bot: target health summary: 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn tg-ingress-euc2
healthy: 31, unhealthy: 4, draining: 0
unhealthy reason: connection-reset, protocol-error
```

maya: Interesting — a small portion unhealthy but overall targets still registered. Reset counts look correlated with specific AZ euc2-b.
ben: Kernel stats on a failing node (euc2-b) show accept queue drops / SYN backlog: 
```
netstat -s | grep SYN
  42000 total connections
  1200 SYN cookies sent
  3400 listen drops
```
claire: That smells like SYN queue / accept backlog exhaustion — maybe Envoy worker threads are saturated or we're hitting somaxconn.

oncall-sre: Running tcpdump on NLB->node shows lots of SYNs then RST from node side. I'm isolating one instance for deeper logs.

maya: Quick mitigation idea: Shift a portion of traffic off euc2 to euc1 via Route53 weighted policy to relieve pressure. Propose 70% -> euc1, 30% remain euc2. Need ops approval.
ben: We can do an immediate traffic split at the Route53 weighted record (ingress.redwood.net). TTL is 60s.

oncall-sre: Doing weight shift now. I’ll create a rollback entry.
ops-bot: ACTION: route53 change submitted by oncall-sre — ingress.redwood.net weight euc1:70 euc2:30. Change ID: ZR53-2615.

claire: Also scaling attempt: increasing pod replicas in euc2 ingress deployment from 4 -> 10 to absorb backlog. Issuing kubectl scale now.
ben: To reduce connection churn, enabling keepalive override on Envoy cluster to 120s on euc2 ingress temporarily.

oncall-sre: After weight shift + scale — error rate dropped to 9% within 2m, then to 3% after 6m. Reset/sec down by ~80% on euc2-b.

maya: Good. Customer-facing impact: some requests experienced 502s for ~8–12 minutes during peak. We'll prepare a note once we have root cause.

infra-bot: Autoscaling events: pod scaled 4 -> 10 at 08:20UTC. Route53 change propagated by 08:21UTC.

ben: Collected dmesg/kern logs from the isolated node — patterns show accept queue overflow then kernel forced RSTs. Snippet: 
```
[ 1234.567890] TCP: possible SYN flooding on port 443. Dropping conn.  Check SNMP counters.
[ 1234.568002] ip_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
```

claire: Looks like backlog + conntrack exhaustion. euc2-b had higher ephemeral port churn — maybe a load tester or noisy client? Any anomalous external spikes?

oncall-sre: Flow logs from AWS show traffic origin IP concentration at a few /24s but requests are valid customers. Could be retry storms from clients when they see 502s.

maya: Short-term: keep route53 weights, keep added pods up, keep Envoy tweaks. Mid-term: increase somaxconn and net.core.somaxconn on nodes and tune conntrack table size on that pool.

ben: I’ll open infra ticket to bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and sysctl tuning across euc2 ASG, with a rollback plan. Ticket INFRA-2615.

oncall-sre: Logs show no codepath regressions; stacktraces from app are clean. This is infra-level.

ops-bot: PagerDuty: Incident assigned to oncall-sre. Acknowledged.

maya: Handoff — @ben will lead infrastructure remediation, @claire will validate application health, I’ll coordinate customer comms. oncall-sre, you can pass to next shift at 09:00UTC.

oncall-sre: Copy. I’ll prepare a short incident summary for the handoff. Current state: degraded -> stable behind traffic shift. No active mitigation tasks required in last 10m. Monitoring closely.

oncall-sre: Incident summary (for handoff):
- Start: 08:12UTC — spike in 5xxs from NLB euc2.
- Impact: ~8–12 minute window with elevated 502/504, affecting ~6% of requests at peak; partial regional impact for euc2.
- Actions: Route53 weighted shift (70%->euc1), ingress pods scaled 4->10 in euc2, Envoy keepalive extended, kernel tuning ticket opened.
- Current: error rate down to baseline (~0.5%). No customer-facing outages ongoing.

claire: For RCA: collect conntrack counters, sysctl state, and correlate client retry patterns. Will run log queries for the impacted minute ranges.

ben: INFRA-2615 created with proposed sysctl: net.core.somaxconn=1024 -> 4096, net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096, net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000. Plan: roll to euc2 ASG in canary then all euc2.

maya: I’ll draft a short customer incident report: timeline + what we did + mitigations to prevent recurrence (tuning + better autoscale for accept queue + an alert for SYN backlog).

oncall-sre: Handoff complete to @ben for remediation and @maya for comms. I’m going offline in 10m. if anything regresses, escalate to pagerduty.

maya: Thanks team. Adding postmortem owner tag: claire. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: INFRA-2615 linked to INCIDENT-2615.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: monitoring continues. Final closure pending RCA.

ben: Post-incident note — no evidence of malicious traffic; root cause appears to be sudden client retry amplification combined with accept queue limits on a subset of nodes. Proposed follow-ups: connection throttling, SYN backlog alerting, and a runbook for rapid weight-shift.

claire: I'll own the RCA doc and include sample queries + dashboards. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD today.

maya: Customer comms drafted and queued for review. Will send once postmortem links are available.
